This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Paris-Lodron Universität Salzburg (PLUS), for the provision of support in Scientific Advisory, online learning resource enhancement, and online & in-person training for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. PLUS will contribute to the online learning resource, training, and Scientific Advisory activities for the overall Service contract, providing niche technical and quality control support to implement resource solutions, contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and support training event implementation and online content maintenance services. PLUS were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought their Department of Geoinformatics into the Service Team, recognized as a hub for graduate education in Geoinformatics with a distinctly international orientation. Next to its rich academic portfolio, this enables the Service to benefit from more than 30 years´ experience in distance learning and postgraduate education for upskilling professionals in geoinformatics and related subjects. PLUS have extensive experience in delivering capacity building activities within and outside Europe, employing a range of Erasmus-supported instruments. For example, the department is the initiator and coordinator of the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master "Copernicus Master in Digital Earth", and they are co-founders of the Copernicus Academy, fostering the emergence of regional and virtual Copernicus hubs. Within the Erasmus Skills Alliance project EO4GEO (2018-2022), they acted as Academic Coordinator to push the Copernicus downstream sector. Additionally, they have engaged in the downstream service evolution for 15+ years in various application areas of interest to the Copernicus community, including biodiversity monitoring, disaster response, and climate change adaptation. This, in addition to their academic portfolio, uniquely places them to contribute to the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – while equipping the Service with their highly beneficial professional networks and Copernicus experience. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

Rammeaftalen tildeles op til 3 leverandører, og tildeling af konkrete rådgivningsopgaver sker ved miniudbud. Der indgås en rammeaftale med hver leverandør. Rammeaftalerne kan ud over Finansministeriet også anvendes af andre enheder i den danske stat. Den danske stat omfatter i denne sammenhæng ministerier, styrelser, direktorater, råd og nævn. Rammeaftalerne er ikke-eksklusiv. Kunden er ikke forpligtet til udelukkende at anvende de indgåede rammeaftaler og er således bl.a. berettiget til at benytte Kammeradvokataftalen samt selv at forestå udførelsen af ydelserne. Dublin City Council intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a suitably qualified service provider to deliver an initial contract for the Dublin Winter Lights Festival. The Dublin Winter Lights Festival has traditionally taken place primarily in outdoor venues and will continue to do so, while also exploring the idea of having some indoor experiences in 2027 and future years. Dublin City Council’s Dublin Winter Lights Festival has illuminated iconic landmarks and more unconventional locations previously, using a range of different projection methods, with more recent years seeing a trend towards full digital projections with locations such as the GPO, Custom House and Collins Barracks seeing full digital video mapping animations. By consistently seeking out innovative and unexpected sites, the festival has continued to evolve and stay fresh. It combines digital art, lighting design, and public performance to illuminate key cultural landmarks across the city, Note: the subject matter of this procurement relates to Title III Services as defined in Directive 2014/24/EU. Please note that this project is subject to funding. The framework agreement will be for a period of six (6) years. The Contracting Authority considers a framework term of six (6) years necessary due to the specialist nature of the services and the significant investment required by the successful Framework Member in artistic lighting infrastructure, projection equipment, storage facilities, specialist personnel, festival development and stakeholder relationships. The longer framework duration is intended to facilitate continuity of service, enable long-term planning and programming of the Dublin City Council Dublin Winter Lights Festival, support the development of artistic partnerships and innovation, and provide value for money through the amortisation of equipment and mobilisation costs over a longer period. The framework will also support the ongoing maintenance, storage and reuse of lighting infrastructure and associated equipment, contributing to sustainability objectives and reducing lifecycle costs. The duration is therefore justified by the subject matter of the framework and the need to secure consistent, high-quality delivery of a flagship cultural event and related artistic lighting projects. The Contracting Authority confirms that the period of any contracts awarded under the framework agreement may extend beyond the date of expiry of the agreement.
